concerns.text: FR-002 requires computing 'average semantic distance' but does not define the metric or the reference space (e.g., embedding model, vector space, or graph distance). Without a definition, this requirement is unverifiable as different implementations yield different results.

FR-004 mandates an 'interpretable classifier' but allows a choice between Random Forest and Logistic Regression. These models have different interpretability mechanisms (feature importances vs. coefficients). The spec must specify which model or define a unified verification procedure for 'interpretability' to ensure the output is checkable.

FR-006 requires a permutation test but does not specify the number of permutations (e.g., 1000 vs 10000). The p-value resolution depends entirely on this count. Without a fixed number, the test is not reproducible or verifiable.

SC-004 states a metric must have a 'non-negligible contribution'. 'Non-negligible' is subjective and not measurable. A specific threshold (e.g., coefficient magnitude > 0.05 or feature importance > 0.01) or a statistical significance test (p < 0.05) is required to make this success criterion verifiable.

SC-005 requires 'all graphs constructed must have valid metric values'. This is a binary pass/fail, but the spec does not define the procedure for handling the 'Edge Case' of empty/short reviews mentioned in User Story 1. If the system assigns default values (0.0) as per the edge case, does that count as 'valid'? The criterion needs to explicitly accept the default-value strategy to be verifiable.
